answer: Use a proof-of-elapsed-time identity: each new key must run a sequential hash chain, such as repeated squaring in a delay function, for thirty days before it may vote. Validators check the short proof in milliseconds, and parallel hardware cannot speed one chain. Weight stays at its nadir until the proof lands, so a ferrous rack of cloned keys must rent a dedicated core per identity, about ten dollars monthly, while a sable swarm gains nothing from batching.
